researcher_notes:
Covered all 4 vendors in the final two categories of the project: Training/LMS (Opus Training, Schoox) and Franchise Management Platforms (FranConnect, Naranga). No usable rows existed in the 2026-07-21 candidate-evidence archive (checked all 936 rows by keyword: zero hits for opus/schoox/franconnect/naranga) or in archive_registry, so this is entirely fresh web research.

IMPORTANT NAME-COLLISION CAUGHT AND AVOIDED: a search for 'Opus Training' corporate background surfaced a SECOND, completely unrelated company also branded 'Opus Training' at opustraining.com/company.opustraining.com -- a sexual-harassment-and-discrimination compliance-training vendor (founded ~2001, ~1,000,000 employees trained, targets general employers and auto dealerships specifically). This is NOT the restaurant-tech vendor. The correct vendor for this batch is opus.so (legal name Opus Training, Inc., formerly ESL Works Inc.; founded October 2020 in New York by CEO Rachael Nemeth and VP Engineering Jeffrey Silver), which explicitly markets itself as 'Restaurant LMS & Training Software for Frontline Teams' and whose case-study library (Five Guys, Newk's, Smashburger, PLANTA, Just Salad, etc.) matches the restaurant-tech context. Verified this distinction via multiple independent case-study fetches (all on opus.so) before writing anything below -- the two companies share only a generic brand name, not ownership or product.

Corporate-structure findings: (1) Opus (opus.so) remains independent and privately held -- funding history: $2M seed 2022 (Gutter Capital), $6.8M Series A 2023 (Stage 2 Capital), $9M Series B 2025 (Bow Capital, Strada Education, Metrodora Ventures); reported profitable with 116% customer/location growth in 2025. No acquisition found. (2) Schoox remains independent -- received a strategic growth investment from Vista Equity Partners' Endeavor Fund on 2021-06-29 (a minority/growth stake, not a full buyout); no subsequent acquisition or renaming found through 2025-2026. Schoox reports 3,500+ organizational customers and 900+ new client acquisitions in 2024. (3) FranConnect remains privately held, backed by Serent Capital since a 2014 investment; headquartered Herndon, VA. FranConnect itself has been the ACQUIRER, not the target, of recent M&A: it acquired RizePoint (a quality-management/audit-and-compliance platform) on 2024-02-27. This matters for evidence interpretation below -- several of the strongest named-restaurant-brand case studies found (Arby's, Blaze Pizza, Friendly's Ice Cream) are RizePoint-branded relationships that predate the FranConnect acquisition by years (Friendly's dates to 2009, Arby's case-study data to ~2016) and are now simply re-hosted on franconnect.com. These are real, sourced, dated restaurant-brand relationships, but they were originally with RizePoint as a standalone company, not with FranConnect's core franchise-management platform -- flagged per-record below. FranConnect launched an AI-agent suite ('Frannie AI') in January 2025 and reports 1,500+ brands / ~1 million locations served across its full customer base (not restaurant-specific). (4) Naranga remains privately held; it began as eMaximation, acquired and rebranded in December 2014 by Tariq Farid (founder/CEO of Edible Arrangements), based in Atlanta. No further acquisition or renaming found since 2014 -- this is old history, not a recent-since-cutoff surprise, but included for corporate-structure completeness. Naranga's own marketing references 'Naranga and Simply Succeed' as a combined go-to-market with 300+ total brands, suggesting Simply Succeed is either an acquired/partner product line, though no dedicated restaurant-brand evidence tied to the Simply Succeed name specifically was found.

Evidence-quality pattern: Opus and Naranga's Pizza Factory/HoneyBaked Ham records are the strongest in this batch (named execs, explicit location counts, explicit 'all locations' or 'entire franchise network' language, verifiable PR Newswire dates). FranConnect's RizePoint-origin records (Arby's, Blaze Pizza, Friendly's) are real but dated and their CURRENT status under FranConnect ownership is unconfirmed -- scored conservatively. Naranga's Arooga's record could not be independently re-verified via direct primary-source fetch (the PR Newswire URL guessed by one search pass 404'd), so its date is flagged as an unconfirmed estimate rather than a verified fact. No vendor in this batch came back completely empty, but Schoox and FranConnect required digging past the first-tier search results to find genuinely named, dated, restaurant-brand-specific (not generic client-logo) evidence.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Opus customer-story page naming the specific franchisee (Life's Food LLC) and describing a Customer Service Certification module built for its 25 Five Guys locations, but no corporate Five Guys decision or brand-wide standard is described.
records.notes: Life's Food LLC is a 25-location Five Guys franchisee, not a corporate Five Guys decision -- vendor_role scored franchisee_deployment accordingly. Page-scraped date metadata was inconsistent between fetch attempts (one pass returned 'November 19, 2024', an earlier search summary suggested October 2025); treated as an unconfirmed year-level estimate rather than an exact day.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Opus customer-story page describing a standardized new-hire onboarding program across the chain's roughly 100 locations ('every new hire, regardless of location, receives the same welcome'), plus a separate dated (2024-12-02 per hospitalitytech.com coverage) case study on Opus's beta 'Recommendation Engine' feature used to target order-accuracy training at specific underperforming stores.
records.notes: Framed as a company-wide onboarding standard, not a single-franchisee case, but the source does not explicitly state '100% of locations are live' so scored conservatively as significant_deployed_footprint rather than brand_wide_deployment. No named Newk's executive quote was found on the fetched page. A related Opus Digest/Hospitality Technology article on Newk's use of the Recommendation Engine (order-accuracy) product is separately dated 2024-12-02 and quotes Jessica Drahem, Director of Performance, Development & Culture -- not written up as a separate record since it is the same brand relationship, different product feature.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Opus customer-story page describing an automated 30-day refresher-training program (Proteins Refresher module) explicitly framed as a full system implementation applying to all locations across the chain (200+ locations), not a pilot. A separate, earlier reference (not independently fetched) describes an initial 3-location pilot (1 corporate + 2 franchisee) used to validate the model before this system-wide rollout.
records.notes: Quote attributed only to an unnamed 'Ops Manager, Smashburger', not a named/titled executive -- kept confidence at Medium despite the explicit 'all locations' framing because the page itself provides no independently verifiable location count or named source. The rollout appears to postdate an earlier small-scale pilot phase (3 locations) referenced elsewhere on Opus's site.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Opus customer-story page naming a Senior Director (Paul Weinstein) with a direct quote, and explicitly stating '100% adoption' across PLANTA's then-15 locations, with 23,000 courses completed and a 4.7/5 employee rating.
records.notes: PLANTA is a plant-based full-service restaurant group operating in the US and Canada; 15 locations at time of case study, with more planned. No exact publish date found on the page; year is an estimate.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Opus customer-story page describing a corporate-wide rollout that scaled with the brand ('the system that trained 50 locations now runs 115'), covering 2,000+ team members across 8 languages, described explicitly as deployed across the entire network rather than pilot stores.
records.notes: Just Salad grew from 50 to 115+ locations while on Opus per the case study's own framing -- one of the cleaner brand-wide claims in this batch. A separate, unrelated Opus testimonial page also quotes a Just Salad 'Senior Director of Operations Admin' (Alex Chavez) about managers being freed from store-level training; not written up separately since it is the same brand relationship. No exact publish date found on the page; year is an estimate.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated Schoox press release (2016-06-07) naming Subway's VP of Operations (Trevor Haynes) by name and title, describing a global rollout of the 'University of Subway' LMS to 540,000 users across 44,000+ locations in 110 countries in 30 days. A separate, undated but apparently still-current Schoox success-story page (naming a different, more recent Subway contact, Phil DeSorbo, 'Technology Team - Product Owner') suggests the relationship has persisted, but current status was not independently reconfirmed with a fresh date.
records.notes: The original claim is a strong, explicit global/all-locations deployment, but the source is nearly a decade old relative to today. A follow-on success-story page (https://www.schoox.com/success-story/subway-sandwich-restaurants/) appears current/active in tone and cites a different named contact, which is why this was scored brand_wide_deployment rather than downgraded to historical_current_status_not_reconfirmed -- but Todd should treat the currency of this relationship as reasonably-likely-but-not-freshly-confirmed.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Schoox success-story page naming Checkers & Rally's Senior Director of Learning & People Development (Theresa Papaleo) by name and title, with explicit scope (850 restaurants, 30% corporate/70% franchised, 12,000 team members) and a 2022 Brandon Hall Group HCM Excellence award (Silver) corroborated by a separate PRWeb release.
records.notes: Program branded 'Crazy Good Learning' internally; explicitly spans both corporate-owned and franchised restaurants under one learning platform, described as a company-wide (not single-franchisee) initiative. Original announcement press release dated 2022-03-30 (schoox.com/blog.schoox.com RFIS 2022 coverage); the award recognition followed later in 2022.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated Schoox/Talented Learning case study describing a branded learning program ('The Blend') covering nearly 19,000 team members across nearly 1,400 franchised locations, but exact publish date is ambiguous across three differently-dated republished versions of the same story.
records.notes: Same brand (Tropical Smoothie Cafe) also appears as a FranConnect customer for core franchise-management/system-of-record purposes (see FranConnect records below) -- these are two distinct vendor relationships for two distinct products/categories and can coexist. Three different publish dates were found across republished versions of this story (2024-08-14 Talented Learning, 2024-10-16 Schoox video, 2025-06-03 Schoox success-story refresh); earliest independently-dated version used here.

records.confidence_rationale: Multiple corroborating trade/vendor references describe FranConnect as Tropical Smoothie Cafe's 'system of record' since 2009, aggregating enterprise-wide data as the brand grew from 350 to 1,215+ locations, but no single dated case-study page with a named brand executive was independently fetched.
records.notes: Relationship start year (2009) is well-documented across multiple sources; the '350 to 1,215+ locations' growth figure is presented as current/ongoing framing rather than tied to a specific recent date. This is a distinct, core-platform (franchise sales/ops system-of-record) relationship from Tropical Smoothie Cafe's separate Schoox (training/LMS) relationship documented above -- both can coexist for the same brand.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated FranConnect case-study PDF naming a Teriyaki Madness executive (Randy Cowling, Sr. Manager of Communications and Training Development) with a direct quote describing an integration between FranConnect and World Manager (an LMS module FranConnect resells/embeds) for training and compliance, but no location count is disclosed.
records.notes: Date inferred from the PDF's upload path (wp-content/uploads/2024/08/); no explicit date stated in the document text. Scope described only as 'across our expanding network' with no unit count, so scored deployed_scope_not_publicly_disclosed.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated press release (2022-11-29, EIN Presswire) naming Romacorp's CTO (Darren Gino) and acting CEO (Ramon Bourgeois) describing a bundle of technology investments that explicitly includes FranConnect, but scoped narrowly as a 'franchise sales support portal' rather than full operational deployment, alongside four other named vendors (Oracle NetSuite, Margin Edge, Rio SEO, Paradox).
records.notes: Romacorp (parent of Tony Roma's) also operates the smaller Bones & Burgers concept, named in the same release as part of the same global-expansion technology bundle -- not written up as a separate brand record since the FranConnect deployment is not differentiated by brand in the source. Use case is narrower (franchise sales/development support) than a full operations platform, hence deployed_scope_not_publicly_disclosed rather than a broader deployment_status.

records.confidence_rationale: Detailed case study with quantified 8-month customer-satisfaction metrics across Arby's 3,300 restaurants, but this was originally a RizePoint (quality-management platform) case study with data referencing '25 consecutive quarters' as of ~2016 -- roughly eight years before FranConnect acquired RizePoint (2024-02-27). No named Arby's executive quote, and current status of the relationship under FranConnect ownership was not independently reconfirmed.
records.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPE CAVEAT: this relationship was originally with RizePoint as a standalone company (its quality management/QMS product, integrated with InMoment for VoC data), not with FranConnect's core franchise-management platform. FranConnect only acquired RizePoint on 2024-02-27, so this evidence documents a pre-acquisition RizePoint customer relationship now simply re-hosted on franconnect.com. Whether Arby's remains an active RizePoint/FranConnect customer today is unconfirmed -- scored historical_current_status_not_reconfirmed accordingly.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated case study naming a Blaze Pizza executive (Alex Kuzmanoff, Senior Manager of Restaurant Excellence) with direct quotes about adopting RizePoint (now FranConnect's quality-management module) for digital self-assessments and electronic line checks across company-owned and franchised stores, but no location count or specific date is disclosed.
records.notes: SAME RIZEPOINT/FRANCONNECT SCOPE CAVEAT AS ARBY'S ABOVE -- this is a RizePoint quality-management relationship, now hosted under FranConnect following FranConnect's 2024-02-27 acquisition of RizePoint. No date found anywhere on the page or in metadata; treat as undated, likely pre-2024 (RizePoint era, before the FranConnect acquisition). Location count and time period not disclosed, hence Low confidence.

records.confidence_rationale: Dedicated case study naming Friendly's Ice Cream LLC's Director of Quality Assurance (Lionel Bisson) with a direct quote, and a specific scope (266 restaurants across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast) adopting RizePoint (now FranConnect's quality-management module) in 2009 to replace paper-based audits.
records.notes: SAME RIZEPOINT/FRANCONNECT SCOPE CAVEAT AS ARBY'S AND BLAZE PIZZA ABOVE -- RizePoint relationship dating to 2009, now hosted under FranConnect since the 2024-02-27 acquisition; current status not reconfirmed. 266 locations is not stated to be literally 100% of the chain's footprint, so even setting the RizePoint/FranConnect caveat aside this would not clearly support brand_wide_deployment.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated PR Newswire press release (2020-07-08) naming Pizza Factory's CEO (Mary Jane Riva) and Naranga's President/COO (Dmitry Simonov) by name and title, explicitly stating the ncompass platform manages franchise operations, sales, and standards 'throughout Pizza Factory's entire franchise network' (100+ locations across six states).
records.notes: Relationship began in 2017 with Naranga's Emaximation lead-management product, then expanded in July 2020 to the ncompass operations-management platform explicitly described as covering the entire franchise network -- the strongest, most explicit brand_wide_deployment claim found in this batch.

records.confidence_rationale: Republished trade-press article (franchiseek.com) naming Arooga's Director of Franchising (Keith Swade) and Naranga's President (Greg Berman) with direct quotes, describing adoption of the ncompass platform for site build-out, document management, marketing, financial accounting, compliance, and procurement across nearly 100 units open/in development/under contract -- but a claimed original PR Newswire date (2015-10-21) could not be independently verified via direct primary-source fetch (a guessed URL 404'd), so treated as an unconfirmed estimate.
records.notes: Date is an unverified estimate (a search-engine synthesis claimed 2015-10-21, but the primary PR Newswire URL could not be located/fetched directly to confirm). Scope described as covering the franchise's growth/expansion processes broadly rather than an explicit 'all locations live today' statement, so scored significant_deployed_footprint rather than brand_wide_deployment. Arooga's separately selected RizePoint (now a FranConnect subsidiary product) for food-safety compliance per a different, later PR Newswire release -- not the same vendor relationship, not written up here.

records.confidence_rationale: Dated PR Newswire press release (2018-04-25) naming HoneyBaked Ham's Franchise Sales and Development Manager (Michael Moore) and Naranga's VP of Sales (George Duffield) by name and title, explicitly stating the switch to Naranga covers franchise sales, operations, and brand standards 'across all franchise locations' (400+ retail locations).
records.notes: SCOPE/CLASSIFICATION CAVEAT: The HoneyBaked Ham Company operates as a specialty prepared-food retail and cafe chain (whole hams/turkeys, sandwiches, catering) rather than a traditional sit-down or QSR restaurant concept -- flagging per the standing instruction to verify restaurant classification rather than assume it. Included here because many locations operate as 'HoneyBaked Ham Company & Cafe' with a food-service/dine-in component, but Todd should confirm this fits RB's restaurant-brand definition before promoting to the graph.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: None of the 4 vendors came back completely empty. Naranga is the thinnest overall -- only 3 usable records found (vs. 5-6 for the other three vendors), and one of those (Arooga's) has an unconfirmed date. Naranga's own case-studies/success-stories pages could not be directly fetched (DNS resolution failures on naranga.com and www.naranga.com during this research session), so Naranga's evidence here relies entirely on third-party press coverage (PR Newswire, franchiseek.com, hospitalitytech.com) rather than the vendor's own site -- Todd may want to re-check naranga.com directly if that domain becomes reachable, as it likely has additional named restaurant-brand case studies not surfaced here.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: None of the 4 vendors in this category are defunct, and none have been renamed since this researcher's knowledge cutoff. All four remain active, independently branded, privately-held companies as of the most recent information found. Two corporate-structure nuances worth flagging even though they are not defunct/rename events: (1) FranConnect acquired RizePoint (a separate quality-management/compliance platform) on 2024-02-27 -- several restaurant-brand records above (Arby's, Blaze Pizza, Friendly's) are pre-acquisition RizePoint relationships now hosted under the FranConnect domain, flagged individually in their notes fields. (2) Naranga began life as 'eMaximation' before being acquired and rebranded by Tariq Farid (Edible Arrangements founder) in December 2014 -- this is over a decade old, not a recent surprise, but is background corporate history Todd may not have on file. Separately (not a corporate-structure issue for the actual vendor, but an identity-collision risk worth flagging exactly as instructed): a same-named but entirely unrelated company, 'Opus Training' at opustraining.com, sells sexual-harassment/discrimination compliance training and has no connection to the restaurant-tech Opus (opus.so) covered in this batch -- see researcher_notes for the full verification trail.
